passos.valor: Objetivo: encontrar numerador X tal que 9/6 = X/4

passos.acao: Simplificar ou converter 9/6 para forma decimal ou mista para facilitar comparação
Dividir a Linha 2 em 4 partes iguais (denominador alvo)
Localizar o ponto equivalente a 1,5 na Linha 2 dividida em quartos
Digitar o numerador 6 no campo R1_user
Selecionar o sinal de igualdade entre as frações

erros.devolutiva: Praticar conversão de frações impróprias para decimais com cálculo explícito antes de marcar na reta
Destacar visualmente os dois inteiros na reta: sombrear 4/4 no primeiro e 2/4 no segundo, totalizando 6/4
Contar intervalos, não marcas: destacar com cores os segmentos entre as marcas

dicas.texto: Boa pergunta! Se duas frações representam o mesmo ponto na reta numérica, o que isso diz sobre elas? Pense: são iguais ou diferentes?
Você está no caminho certo! Primeiro, observe onde 9/6 está na Linha 1. Depois, divida a Linha 2 em 4 partes iguais entre 0 e 1, e continue até 2. Veja em qual marcação o ponto cai.
Quase lá! 9/6 é maior que 1. Na Linha 2 dividida em quartos, quantos quartos estão entre 1 e 1½? Conte os espaços!
Você está muito perto! 9/6 = 1 e 3/6 = 1,5. Na Linha 2 com quartos, 1,5 fica exatamente entre 1 e 2. Quantos quartos dão 1,5? Pense: 4/4 = 1, então 6/4 = ?
Lembre-se: frações equivalentes ocupam a mesma posição na reta. Se você sabe onde está 9/6, como encontrar essa mesma posição com quartos?
Ótimo! Conte os quartos a partir do zero: 1/4, 2/4, 3/4, 4/4 (=1), 5/4, 6/4... Pare quando chegar à mesma altura de 9/6.
Veja bem: 9/6 = 3/2 = 1,5. Em quartos, 1,5 é igual a quantos quartos? Dica: 1 = 4/4, então 1,5 = 4/4 + 2/4.
Você quase chegou! Se 1 inteiro tem 4 quartos, então 1 inteiro e meio tem 4 + 2 = ? quartos. Digite esse número no numerador!

hints.message: Look at the marked point and connect its position with the equal parts shown on Line 1.
Count the marked intervals from zero for the numerator, then count the equal intervals in one whole for the denominator.
The marked point is beyond one whole, so count every sixth up to that point instead of stopping at the first whole.
Record the total number of marked sixths above the line and place it over the number of sixths in one whole.

nodes.description: Manipulate the model to express 9/6 as a mixed number.
nodes.instruction: Manipulate the model to express 9/6 as a mixed number.

hints.message: A fraction greater than one can be separated into complete wholes and a remaining fractional part.
Take one full group equal to the denominator, then simplify the remaining fraction.
Use six sixths for the complete whole and examine the three sixths that remain.
Write one whole, then replace the remaining three sixths with the equivalent half before combining the two parts.

nodes.description: Enter the target denominator and confirm the division of Line 2.
nodes.instruction: Enter the target denominator and confirm the division of Line 2.

hints.message: The denominator tells how many equal parts make one whole on the new number line.
Read the unit named in the question and enter that number in the denominator field.
The target unit is different from the sixths on Line 1; use the number of parts named by the target unit.
Set the denominator field to the number of equal intervals required for each whole, then press confirm.

misconceptions.description: Aluno confunde 'fourths' com 'halves' e divide a reta em 2 partes em vez de 4
misconceptions.feedback: You divided the line into halves. The target unit means four equal parts in each whole, not two.

misconceptions.description: Aluno ignora o pedido por 'fourths' e repete o denominador original
misconceptions.feedback: You copied the denominator from Line 1. Line 2 must use the new unit requested in the question.

nodes.description: Mark the point on Line 2 that represents the same amount.
nodes.instruction: Mark the point on Line 2 that represents the same amount.

hints.message: Equivalent fractions mark the same position on a number line even when their denominators differ.
Locate one whole first, then use the equal fourth-sized intervals to find the remaining half.
The target lies halfway between 1 and 2, so count the fourths from zero through the first whole and the remaining part.
Count four fourths to reach 1 and two more fourths to reach the marked position, then place the point there.

misconceptions.description: Aluno conta quantas marcas até o ponto (3) e assume que é o numerador, sem considerar que o inteiro tem 4 partes → responde 3/4, mas o valor real é 6/4 | Aluno lê a barra de fração como sinal de subtração | Aluno lê a barra de fração como sinal de subtração
misconceptions.feedback: You counted the distance within the second part but forgot the four fourths already contained in the first whole. (Ou, se foi por outro motivo: The slash means division, not subtraction. Read 9/6 as nine divided by six before locating its position.) misconceptions.description: Aluno julga a posição pela 'distância até o próximo inteiro' (gap thinking): vê que 9/6 = 1.5, mas pensa 'falta pouco para 2', então marca mais perto do 2
misconceptions.feedback: You judged the point by the gap to the next whole. Use the exact equal intervals instead of estimating the remaining distance.

misconceptions.description: Aluno trata cada marca da reta como unidade inteira e coloca o ponto na nona marca, ignorando a escala real (0 a 2)
misconceptions.feedback: You used the original numerator as a position. On Line 2, each interval represents one fourth, so the scale must be read in fourths.

misconceptions.description: Aluno aproxima o valor para o inteiro mais próximo e ignora a parte fracionária
misconceptions.feedback: You moved the point to the nearest whole. Keep the exact halfway position instead of rounding.

nodes.description: Enter the numerator of the equivalent fraction shown on the right.
nodes.instruction: Enter the numerator of the equivalent fraction shown on the right.

hints.message: The numerator counts how many parts of the new denominator reach the marked amount.
Count the fourths from zero to the marked point, including the complete first whole.
There are four fourths in the first whole and two additional fourths in the remaining half.
Combine the four parts from the whole with the two parts beyond it, and enter that total in R1_user.

misconceptions.description: Aluno assume que o numerador permanece o mesmo ao mudar o denominador
misconceptions.feedback: You repeated the original numerator. Changing from sixths to fourths changes how many parts represent the same amount.

misconceptions.description: Aluno simplifica a fração, mas não a converte para o denominador pedido
misconceptions.feedback: You used the numerator from the simplified fraction 3/2. The requested fraction must be written in fourths.

misconceptions.description: Aluno tenta usar regra de três, mas inverte a relação entre numerador e denominador
misconceptions.feedback: You treated the target denominator as the numerator. Keep track of which number counts parts and which number names their size.

misconceptions.description: Aluno vê 1.5 como 'meio' e associa a 2/4, esquecendo o inteiro completo
misconceptions.feedback: You counted only the two fourths in the remaining half and left out the four fourths in the complete whole.

misconceptions.description: Aluno conta as marcas incluindo o zero ou erra a contagem dos intervalos, obtendo 7 em vez de 6
misconceptions.feedback: You counted one interval too many. Count the spaces between marks, starting at zero, rather than counting the endpoint twice.

nodes.description: Use the comparison selector to state the relationship between the two fractions.
nodes.instruction: Use the comparison selector to state the relationship between the two fractions.

hints.message: Equivalent fractions represent the same quantity, even when the numbers of parts are different.
Compare the positions marked on Line 1 and Line 2 rather than comparing the numerators and denominators separately.
The two marked points coincide at the same location between 1 and 2.
Choose the symbol that says both sides have the same value.

misconceptions.description: Aluno duvida da equivalência e escolhe 'não igual' como resposta conservadora
misconceptions.feedback: The two fractions mark the same point, so they represent the same amount rather than different amounts.

misconceptions.description: Aluno não reconhece que deve escolher '=' após concluir a equivalência
misconceptions.feedback: The question symbol leaves the relationship undecided. After matching the points, select the symbol for equal values.

nodes.description: Manipulate the Done button to complete the problem.
nodes.instruction: Manipulate the Done button to complete the problem.

hints.message: Before finishing, check that the two fractions represent the same point on the number lines.
Review the denominator, the marked point, the numerator field, and the comparison selector.
Make sure Line 2 uses fourths and that the comparison shows the same-value relationship.
When every field and mark agrees with the two number lines, press the Done button to submit.
